edges.notes: Linux namespaces are kernel mechanisms for isolating views of global resources (mount, UTS, IPC, PID, network, user, cgroup, time per documented types).
Docker Engine on Linux composes namespaces (and cgroups) for container isolation per common deployment understanding.
Kubernetes pods and containers rely on Linux namespaces on Linux nodes.
containerd creates and joins namespaces when managing Linux containers.
runc configures Linux namespaces when creating OCI runtime bundles on Linux.
Podman uses Linux namespaces for rootless and rootful containers on Linux.
CRI-O configures Linux namespaces for Kubernetes workloads on Linux nodes.
systemd may create or enter namespaces for services and portable/nspawn-style flows on Linux.
Linux container isolation commonly composes namespaces with cgroup resource controllers; distinct concerns.
Container stacks compose namespaces with capability sets; namespaces change views, capabilities gate privileged operations.
Mount namespaces scope overlay union mounts; OverlayFS is a filesystem driver, not a namespace kind.
Network namespaces scope interfaces and routing; netfilter rules are evaluated per network namespace.
Mount namespaces scope FUSE mounts; FUSE is a filesystem mechanism, not a namespace kind.
Namespaces isolate process views within one kernel; KVM runs separate guest VMs — different isolation model.
